summary: Reserved pool inference lag: intermittent GPU page-fault spikes and scheduler affinity flapping
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteForge is experiencing sustained p95/p99 inference latency regressions and increased 504 timeouts across a reserved dedicated pool (reservation-id: res-cedar-09) starting 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC. Impact: noteforge production route note-gen (qps ~18) saw p95 increase from ~120ms to 800-2,400ms and ~6% request timeouts. Only requests pinned to the reserved pool are affected.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation res-cedar-09, pool size configured min=2,max=6 (instance type: gpuslice-8xA100-80GB logical partitions)
- Serving runtime v1.8.3, scheduler v0.7.1, autoscaler v2.1.0
- Region: us-east-1

Observed behaviour / timeline:
- 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC: First customer report of elevated p95.
- 2026-03-09 22:45 UTC: Support confirmed increased 5xx and timeouts on route note-gen and bumped priority to P1.
- 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC: SRE observed intermittent bursts of GPU page-fault counts and NVML reports showing transient PCIe retransmits on two nodes.
- 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: Autoscaler triggered scale-out to 4 GPUs then immediately scaled back to 2 over ~4 minutes; affinity labels for worker pods were re-assigned during this period.
- 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC: Support applied temporary affinity pinning to avoid worker eviction; request latencies improved but regressions recurred under burst traffic.

Initial impact and scope:
- Only requests routed to this dedicated reservation observed the pattern; shared-hosted API unaffected.
- Affects both model variants listed; workload pattern: many short requests with low token counts (mean 18 tokens).

Immediate customer-facing mitigation applied:
- Short-term: increased client-side retry window and 504 -> 502 retry translation to reduce perceived failures.
- Infra: applied node-level affinity pinning and raised autoscaler cooldown from 30s to 180s for this reservation.

Attachments / dashboards referenced:
- Grafana: /d/infra/serving-reservations?var=reservation=res-cedar-09
- DCGM/NVML snapshots: s3://support-logs/sup-217450/dcgm-nvml-20260310.tar.gz
- k8s events and pod logs: s3://support-logs/sup-217450/k8s-events-20260310.log
steps_to_reproduce: Send a steady burst of short inference requests (~20 tokens) at 15-25 qps to customer's reservation endpoint
Observe p95 and p99 on reservation Grafana dashboard and pod-level nvml/dcgm metrics
Replay captured workload with load-generator against a reserved pool replica (test-res-09)
investigation_notes: NVML metrics show repeated spikes in 'page_fault_count' and a correlated rise in PCIe retransmit errors on nodes node-cc-07 and node-cc-08 during latency spikes
Kernel logs on node-cc-07 contain repeated 'GPU page fault' entries and a few 'GPU reset' events in a 10-minute window (not full node crash)
Autoscaler behavior: observed rapid scale-out then immediate scale-in due to combination of short cooldown and transient CPU pressure from background maintenance jobs on the same nodes
Kubernetes scheduler report: pod affinity labels oscillated after scale events, forcing model worker replicas to be rescheduled twice within ~5 minutes
Hypothesis 1: noisy neighbor background processes on host VMs cause transient kernel/GPU driver contention (page faults and PCIe retries) leading to per-pod latency spikes
Hypothesis 2: autoscaler cooldown too short causing frequent pod migrations which exacerbate warm KV cache misses and KV rehydration overhead, increasing per-request tail latency
logs_snippets: [dmesg] 02:09:43 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU page fault on ch 0x4f0a000, but not a fatal error
[kubelet] 02:12:01 eviction: Pod note-worker-7 re-scheduled from node-cc-07 -> node-cc-08 due to affinity update
[autoscaler] 02:11:58 scaled cluster from 2 -> 4, 02:12:40 scaled back 4 -> 2 due to low observed CPU utilization
actions_taken: Applied temporary affinity pinning to keep serving worker pods on current nodes (2026-03-10 04:05 UTC)
Increased autoscaler cooldown for reservation res-cedar-09 from 30s -> 180s (2026-03-10 04:20 UTC)
Opened ticket with infra to investigate host-level background maintenance jobs and noisy processes on node-cc-07/08 (task assigned to infra team)
Disabled a non-critical background image-prepull cron job on affected nodes to reduce host CPU interference (2026-03-10 05:00 UTC)
Collected full DCGM and kernel traces for the timeframe and uploaded to support S3 bucket for postmortem
next_steps: Infra to run hardware-level memory and PCIe health checks on node-cc-07 and node-cc-08 and report findings (ETA 2026-03-14)
Backport driver stability patch to serving-runtime v1.8.x and deploy to a test reservation (PR linked)
Implement sticky-pod scheduling for customer reservations as an opt-in setting to avoid frequent re-schedules during autoscaler churn
Run controlled load replay against a patched test-reservation and validate p99 tail latency under burst traffic (owner: Evan Chu)
comments: Priya Patel (2026-03-10): Customer reported elevated p95 and ~6% 504s. Escalated to SRE and set P1.
Evan Chu (2026-03-10): Collected DCGM and dmesg from nodes; seeing GPU page-fault spikes concurrent with PCIe retransmits. Pinning pods and increasing cooldown as temporary mitigation.
SRE Infra (2026-03-11): Found scheduled Pre-pull cron running heavy image prep on affected nodes between 02:00-02:30 UTC. Disabled cron on reserved-pool nodes and scheduled deeper health checks.
Customer (NoteForge SRE) (2026-03-11): Latency improved after affinity pinning but still see sporadic spikes under production bursts. Thank you for quick mitigation. We need durable fix.
Evan Chu (2026-03-12): Plan to backport scheduler affinity sticky feature and driver hotfix; will coordinate maintenance window for rolling restart of this reservation (proposed 2026-03-16 03:00 UTC)
Support Manager (2026-03-13): Re-opened related incident INC-98123 for postmortem. Recommend customer-facing RCA after infra health checks complete.
Infra (2026-03-13): PCIe health checks passed; vendor recommends kernel upgrade and GPU driver micro-patch to address spurious page-faults under heavy short-lived kernel work.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: temporary affinity pinning and longer autoscaler cooldown reduced occurrence and customer timeouts. Final resolution pending: infra to apply driver/kernel micro-patch and runtime scheduler change to support sticky scheduling for reservations. After patch validation in test reservation and a coordinated maintenance window we will roll the fix to res-cedar-09 and confirm p99 latency returns to baseline. Postmortem and RCA will be published to linked Confluence page.
resolution_notes: If driver patch confirms reduction in page-fault events and sticky scheduling prevents reschedules during short bursts, mark Resolved and follow up with customer on 7-day latency monitoring window. Otherwise, consider reserving dedicated physical GPUs for this enterprise customer as a last-mile mitigation.
priority_notes: Customer is enterprise-tier with SLA obligations for this reserved pool. P1 due to ongoing production impact; extended monitoring for 72h after fix rollout required.
